title: Combustion Boundary Suppression
subtitle: Adaptive Acoustic Sensing with Dielectric-Foam Intervention

concept.method: Adaptive acoustic sensing and counter-pulsing with dielectric-foam deposition
concept.primary_mechanism: Foam-based cooling, isolation, and propagation control

spine.structure: Sense -> estimate -> perturb -> deposit -> measure -> adapt
spine.coherence: Suppression requires agreement among sensing, acoustic intervention, foam delivery, gas conditions, and thermal measurements.
drift: Foam coverage masking unresolved thermal activity

symmetry_shift.to: Externally bounded and thermally controlled state

structural_paradox.description: The acoustic field may function as detector, diagnostic probe, suppressive actuator, or destabilizing input.
structural_paradox.control_requirement: The controller must determine both when to perturb and when not to perturb.
structural_paradox.safe_state: Acoustic silence may sometimes be the correct state.

success_conditions: External combustion reduced or beneficially displaced
Heat removal exceeds continuing heat generation
Stability persists after active acoustic intervention ends
testing_domain: Professional, remote, instrumented fire laboratory only
student_takeaway: The research target is not the flame alone. The target is the transition structure sustaining the event.
final_leaf: Do not fight only the visible flame. Detect the regime, perturb its boundary when beneficial, establish cooling and isolation, and verify that the hidden transition has actually stopped.
